family.name: Niva
family.verdict: A Zhiguli engine, Range Rover-style full-time 4WD and a body the size of a hatchback. It went to Antarctica, the North Pole and Everest base camp, and it's still in production nearly fifty years later.
intro: In the early 1970s the Soviet government asked AvtoVAZ for a car the countryside could actually use. The Niva (VAZ-2121) went into production in Tolyatti on 5 April 1977. It had a unibody, independent front suspension, coil springs all round and full-time four-wheel drive with a lockable centre differential. That last feature was rare in 1977, though the [[range-rover/classic|Range Rover]] had it. Wikipedia calls the Niva the world's first mass-produced off-roader with unibody construction.

The West bought it in big numbers. It was Lada's best-selling export, and Britain had it from 1978 and Canada from the 1981 model year until 1998. Trade sanctions kept it out of the US, which is why American Nivas are 25-year-rule imports. Along the way it became the 1.7 21213 and 21214, grew a five-door VAZ-2131 version, and was renamed Lada 4x4 in 2006 and Lada Niva Legend in 2021.

We cover the whole run on [[niva/niva|one page]], because the 2121 and its descendants are one design that has been updated for almost 50 years rather than replaced. The Chevrolet Niva (VAZ-2123), now sold as the Lada Niva Travel, is a different car.

generations.name: Lada Niva (VAZ-2121 / 4x4 / Niva Legend)

page.title: Lada Niva (VAZ-2121 / 4x4 Legend)
page.verdict: A Soviet farm car with Range Rover-style full-time 4WD, a hatchback's footprint and a cult following. It's crude, rusty and slow, it'll go almost anywhere, and you can fix most of it at home.

paragraphs: At the start of the 1970s, Soviet premier Alexei Kosygin gave the engineers at the brand-new Volga Automobile Plant an awkward job. The Fiat-based Zhiguli was about to put millions of city dwellers on wheels, but it was close to useless on village roads. He wanted a car for the countryside with the comfort of a Zhiguli. VAZ's answer went on sale on 5 April 1977 and has never really stopped. It's been the VAZ-2121, the Lada Niva, the Lada 4x4 and now the Lada Niva Legend, and it still has the same short, upright, slightly startled shape.

story.heading: A RENAULT 5 ON A LAND ROVER CHASSIS
paragraphs: That's how its designers described it, according to Wikipedia, and it's a fair summary. Chief designer Vladimir Solovyov's team started in 1971. The first running prototype, the E-2121, was nicknamed 'krokodil' for its snout, and was rejected as too utilitarian. What followed was a three-door hatchback: unibody, coil springs at every corner, independent front suspension and a live rear axle on five links. Wikipedia calls it the world's first mass-produced off-roader with unibody construction, years before the [[jeep/cherokee-xj|Cherokee XJ]]. The engine and gearbox came from the VAZ-2106; the body, the four-wheel-drive system and the front suspension were VAZ's own.

The drivetrain is the clever part. Like the [[range-rover/classic|Range Rover]], the Niva has full-time four-wheel drive, with three differentials and a two-speed transfer case whose centre differential the driver locks with a second little lever. The front differential bolted to the engine, which needed a deeper sump. Before production, Vadim Kotlyarov's test team drove prototypes through the Urals, Siberia, the Kazakh deserts and the Pamirs, against a UAZ-469, a [[land-rover/series|Land Rover Series]] and a Range Rover. Pyotr Prusov took over after Solovyov died, and the plant later disputed the story that the name was an acronym of the designers' children's names.

story.heading: THE SOVIET UNION'S BEST EXPORT
paragraphs: The Niva was shown at the 1978 Paris salon, and the West took to it. Wikipedia says it quickly took 40% of Europe's four-wheel-drive market and became Lada's best-selling export. Russian Wikipedia says VAZ raised the plan from 25,000 a year to 50,000 and then 70,000 because of demand abroad, while Soviet buyers waited. It was the only Soviet car regularly sold in Japan. Britain got left-hand-drive trucks from November 1978 and right-hand drive from February 1983, and importers dressed them up as the Cossack with roof rails, decals and alloys. In Britain it took on the [[suzuki/samurai|Suzuki SJ]] and was a good deal cheaper.

North America got it too, just not the US. Lada Canada sold the Niva from the 1981 model year, more than 12,000 of them in the first year, and kept it until 1998, the last Lada sold there. Trade sanctions kept Ladas out of the US. Hagerty's Jim Kenzie calls it 'quite capable off-road' and 'extremely agricultural anywhere else', which is about right. Then came the stunts. A Niva worked with the Soviet Antarctic Expedition from 1990 to 2001, covering more than 40,000 km at down to −54 °C. In 1998 a five-door was dropped by parachute near the North Pole, and another drove to Everest base camp at 5,200 m.

story.heading: FORTY-NINE YEARS OF SMALL CHANGES
paragraphs: The big update came in 1993–94. The 21213 got a 1.7, a five-speed gearbox, 3.9 axle ratios in place of 4.3, a deeper tailgate and a VAZ-2108 dashboard. The 21214 added fuel injection, first single-point from GM and later multipoint. A five-door 2131 on a wheelbase 500 mm longer reached series production in 1995, and a Peugeot-diesel 21215 was built for export from 1999 to 2007. In 2006 the old car became the Lada 4x4, because the Niva name went to the GM-AvtoVAZ Chevrolet Niva. In 2002 Russia's ARCAP test gave it zero stars, and Wikipedia said in 2019 that no version had airbags.

Updates kept coming slowly. The 21214M changes of 2009–2011 brought a reworked rear suspension, a new clutch and better brakes, with parts shared with the Chevrolet Niva. ABS arrived in October 2011, and front hub bearings that never need adjusting arrived in October 2016. The plastic-bumpered Urban came in 2014 and the factory-lifted Bronto in 2017. In January 2021 the old car became the Lada Niva Legend. Western sanctions in 2022 briefly stopped the plant, and it came back as a Classic'22 without ABS. Production of the five-door ended in January 2022, Russian Wikipedia says.

story.heading: STILL HERE
paragraphs: Since the [[land-rover/defender-90-110|Defender]] ended in 2016, Wikipedia says the Niva has been the longest-running light off-roader still made in its original form. It isn't finished yet. In June 2026 AvtoVAZ showed another update. It has a 90 hp 1.8 (VAZ-11184), ventilated Vesta front discs, a single transfer-case lever in place of two, and a driver's front airbag in a Granta steering wheel. Production started on 20 July 2026. For Americans the sweet spot is older. Every Niva built more than 25 years ago can now be imported, and the carbureted 1.6 and 1.7 trucks are simple enough to fix with hand tools and patience. That's exactly what the Niva was built for.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE NIVA AT THE ENDS OF THE EARTH
callout.title: Antarctica, the North Pole and 5,725 metres
paragraphs: Wikipedia calls a classic VAZ-2121 the first wheeled vehicle to spend more than ten years in Antarctica. The Soviet Antarctic Expedition used it from 1990 to 2001 to move people and goods, link stations and tow boats. It covered more than 40,000 km at temperatures as low as −54 °C.

The long-wheelbase VAZ-2131 did the rest. In 1998 one was dropped by parachute onto the ice and completed its route to the North Pole at an average −30 °C. The same year another reached Everest base camp at 5,200 m. On 16 September 1999 a St Petersburg expedition team's Niva climbed to 5,725 m on a Tibetan mountain. Not bad for a car designed for collective farms.

page.engineering_intro: The Niva is a unibody with the running gear bolted underneath. A longitudinal four-cylinder from the classic rear-drive Zhiguli family drives a four- or five-speed gearbox. Behind that is a separate two-speed transfer case with a lockable centre differential, which feeds both axles all the time. The front differential, bolted to the engine until 2016, drives the wheels through CV-jointed shafts. The front suspension uses double wishbones and the rear is a live axle on five links, both on coil springs. Most of the parts are shared with other VAZ models, so they're cheap and plentiful in Russia and Eastern Europe, though harder to find in the US.

engineering.note: Wikipedia calls it the first mass-produced off-roader without a separate frame.
Two transfer-case levers (high/low and centre lock) until the 2026 update merged them into one.
The front differential was bolted to the engine until October 2016, when it got its own mounting. Adjustable hub bearings until then too.

The low range is engaged at a standstill; the centre lock and high range can be selected on the move with the clutch down.

buying_checks.head: Rust is the deal-breaker
buying_checks.body: It's a 1970s Soviet unibody, so the body is the chassis. Probe the sills, the jacking points, the floor where the sills join it, and where the rear trailing-arm brackets mount. NIVA-FAQ's sill guide says to tap with a screwdriver and replace anything you can push it through. Most of the BaT Nivas we read noted rust somewhere: under the bonnet, on the undercarriage or in the rear arches.

buying_checks.head: Know which Niva you're buying
buying_checks.body: The VIN starts with XTA (AvtoVAZ), then six characters for the model (212100 is a 2121), a model-year character and a seven-digit serial. Pre-1985 trucks have chrome details and a red-background badge; 1.7 trucks from 1993–94 have vertical tail lights and a tailgate that drops to the bumper. A Chevrolet Niva (VAZ-2123), sold today as the Niva Travel, is a different car.

buying_checks.head: Drive it at 50–70 mph and feel for vibration
buying_checks.body: A shake through the floor at speed is the classic Niva complaint. It usually points to the transfer case's alignment with the propshafts, worn U-joints or dry splines. NIVA-FAQ's centring procedure fixes most of it, but a truck that still shakes may have worn mounts or a bent floor.

buying_checks.head: Work the transfer-case levers
buying_checks.body: Select low range at a standstill, then lock and unlock the centre diff, and check that the dash light comes on. A centre lock that sticks in or won't engage usually needs the steering-wiggle trick from the FAQ below, but it can also point to a neglected transfer case. Owners advise using the levers at least weekly.

buying_checks.head: Listen at cold start
buying_checks.body: A brief rattle or rumble from the top of the engine on a cold start is the timing chain slapping a worn tensioner or guide. It's a known and fixable problem, but price it in. The 1.6 and 1.7 petrol engines have no timing belt to worry about.

buying_checks.head: Check the hubs and the rear axle seals
buying_checks.body: On pre-October-2016 trucks, rock each front wheel for bearing play; the bearings need periodic adjustment. Oil on the inside of a rear wheel or on the brake backing plate means a leaking axle seal or bearing, and the brake shoes are probably soaked.

buying_checks.head: Get the import paperwork
buying_checks.body: US Nivas arrived from Spain, the Netherlands, Estonia, Russia and Canada, according to BaT listings. You want the CBP entry papers, the EPA and DOT forms, and a clean title in your state. Expect a km/h speedometer and Cyrillic gauges on Soviet-market trucks.

buying_checks.head: Treat the carburettor and fuel system as suspect
buying_checks.body: BaT sellers of imported 1.6s report replacing the fuel tank, sender, carburettor and plug leads after the trucks had sat. Budget for a carb rebuild or replacement and a new tank on any truck that has been parked for years.

repairs.title: Timing chain, tensioner and guide (shoe) replacement
repairs.time: ≈ A day for the full chain set
repairs.symptoms: A rattle or rumble from the top of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, which gets more persistent as the chain and guides wear. One NIVA-FAQ owner found that his mechanics recognised the noise straight away as a warning of serious trouble.
repairs.fix: With the cam cover off, inspect the chain damper and tensioner shoe. Some owners tie the chain to the cam sprocket with wire so it can't jump off. For a tensioner-only fix on the 21214, owners fit an automatic chain tensioner such as the 'Pilot' (with the longer plunger for the Niva, not the short one for the classic Zhiguli) and set it to the maker's instructions, then fit a new cam-cover gasket. On a worn engine, replace the chain, sprockets, damper and shoe together. Use the correct shoe: NIVA-FAQ contributors say the 2103-type shoe suits the 2121 engine and the 2101 type doesn't fit properly. Set the timing marks and torques from the factory manual.
repairs.tools: Socket set · torque wrench · wire to hold the chain · gasket sealant · new cam-cover gasket (one owner switched to cork after the rubber one leaked).

repairs.title: Cure driveline vibration: U-joints, splines and transfer-case centring
repairs.symptoms: Vibration or a hum through the floor at speed, usually worst at one road speed. It's the Niva's signature fault.
repairs.fix: Start with the cheap things: balance the wheels, then check and grease the propshaft U-joints and slip splines (the factory schedule greases them every 10,000 km), and replace any notchy joint. Then centre the transfer case dynamically, as NIVA-FAQ describes. Set the mounts so the studs sit in the middle of their slots, put the transfer case in high range with the centre diff unlocked, and loosen its four mounting nuts just enough for it to move. Run the truck in fourth or fifth at the speed where it vibrates (owners use 60–110 km/h) and nudge the case sideways, never fore and aft, while a helper underneath retightens the nuts. Only do this with the truck securely supported on a lift, a pit or stands under the suspension arms. A VAZ-2121 needs shims under the mounts to set the height first; 21213-on trucks use a CV-jointed intermediate shaft, which removed that adjustment.
repairs.tools: Lift, pit or proper stands · grease gun · sockets · hammer handle to nudge the case · a careful helper.

repairs.title: Adjust and regrease the front hub bearings (pre-October 2016)
repairs.symptoms: Play when you rock the wheel top to bottom, a knock over bumps, or a hub that runs hot. The factory schedule checks the play at every service and repacks and readjusts the bearings at 40,000 km.
repairs.fix: Remove the hub cap and the staked hub nut, and clean the threads. Fit a new nut and tighten it hard while turning the wheel. Then back it off a little at a time, spinning the wheel each time, until a slight play and a faint knock appear. Tighten it again just enough to remove the play, without overtightening. With the brake pads backed off and the axle oil warm, a correctly set wheel spins and coasts to a gentle stop. Stake the nut collar into the groove in two places. Trucks built from October 2016 have bearings that don't need adjusting, and some owners convert older trucks with the 2016 knuckles and hubs.
repairs.tools: Large socket for the hub nut · blunt chisel and hammer to stake the nut · bearing grease · new hub nuts.

repairs.title: Rear axle shaft bearing and seal
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the inside of the rear wheel and brake backing plate, oily shoes and weak rear brakes, or a growl from one rear corner.
repairs.fix: Pull the axle shaft; a slide hammer helps, because water running off the backing plate can seize the bearing ring in place. The bearing is held on by a pressed-on locking ring. NIVA-FAQ contributors cut the old ring with a hacksaw (or very carefully with a grinder) and split it with a chisel. They heat the new ring to about 300–400 °C on a gas burner, slide it on square with a wire holder and seat it with a tube drift. Replace the seal and, if they're oil-soaked, the brake shoes. Run sealant around the backing plate where it meets the axle housing to keep water out.
repairs.tools: Slide hammer · bench vice · hacksaw · chisel · gas burner and wire holder · tube drift and sledgehammer · sealant.

repairs.title: Front CV joint boots and joints
repairs.symptoms: Grease flung around the inside of the front wheel from a split boot, then clicking on full lock under power as the outer joint wears.
repairs.fix: The Niva's front driveshafts use CV joints at both ends, like a front-wheel-drive car. Replace a split boot before dirt kills the joint. Remove the driveshaft (VAZ's TI 3100.25100.20038 covers removal and TI 3100.25100.20045 covers boot replacement), clean the joint, repack it with CV grease and fit the new boot and clamps. Buy joints to match your axle: in 2004 VAZ began fitting joints with more splines (Z = 24) on the 21213 family.
repairs.tools: Hub-nut socket · ball-joint separator · circlip pliers · CV grease · boot clamp pliers.

repairs.title: Ball joints and front shocks
repairs.symptoms: A clunk over bumps, vague steering or uneven front tyre wear. The factory schedule checks the ball joints, arm bushes and shocks at every service.
repairs.fix: Support the lower arm, because the coil spring sits on it. Separate the ball joint tapers and unbolt the old joints from the arms, then bolt in the new ones and torque them to the factory figures. NIVA-FAQ has a guide to changing the joints without spring compressors. While you're there, replace tired shocks and check the arm bushes. Have the alignment checked afterwards; VAZ publishes separate alignment data for the 21214M.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · ball-joint separator · sockets · torque wrench.

parts.name: Front and rear Sachs shocks, Niva 2121 78–98

repairs.title: Sill (rocker) replacement
repairs.symptoms: Bubbling paint along the bottom of the doors, soft jacking points, or a screwdriver that goes through the inner sill.
repairs.fix: On a unibody this is structural, so brace the body before cutting. NIVA-FAQ's guide explains that each sill has three layers: the outer panel, an inner connector joined to the floor, and a reinforcement. The jacking points and the bracket for the rear trailing arm are welded to the inside. Remove the doors and seats, support the middle of the body, cut out the rot in stages, inspect the floor and rails where the brackets join, and weld in new metal. Then wax the cavities, because VAZ's own schedule includes a yearly anti-corrosion inspection and clearing the sill drain holes at every service.
repairs.tools: MIG welder · angle grinder · spot-weld drill · body supports · cavity wax.

repairs.title: Carburettor service (1.6 and carbureted 1.7)
repairs.symptoms: Hard starting, a flat spot, poor idle or heavy fuel use. Imports that have stood for years usually have varnished carbs and rusty tanks.
repairs.fix: Early 2121s use a Weber-type (DAAZ) twin-choke carburettor and 21213s use a Solex-type 2108-family unit; NIVA-FAQ has strip-down and adjustment guides for both. Fit a new fuel filter, then strip and clean the carb, check the float level and jets, replace the gaskets and set the idle. If the tank is rusty, replace it, or you'll be cleaning the carb again within weeks. A new carburettor is often the faster fix; one BaT seller replaced the tank, sender, carb and plug leads on an imported 1.6.
repairs.tools: Screwdrivers · carb cleaner · gasket kit · rev counter.

baseline_service.intro: Assume nothing has been done unless there are receipts, especially on an import that sat before it crossed an ocean. Specs here are from AvtoVAZ's own owner's manuals (2008 and 2018 editions) and the 2013 service book for the injected 1.7 21214. Capacities for a 1.6 VAZ-2121 or a carbureted 21213 may differ slightly, so check your engine. One more Niva quirk: grease the propshafts and check the front hub bearings far more often than you're used to.

items.spec: API SL/SM/SN; SAE grade by climate (e.g. 5W-40 or 10W-40) · 3.75 L (≈4.0 US qt) with filter
items.note: AvtoVAZ's table runs from 0W-30 below −35 °C starts to 20W-50 in heat.

items.interval: Inspect at baseline; listen at every cold start
items.note: A rattle at start-up means the tensioner or guide is worn. See the repair above.

items.interval: Every 30,000 km (≈18,600 mi); sooner in dust

items.note: On a long-stored import, check the tank for rust and sediment as well.

items.spec: A17DVRM (Bosch Saratov), Brisk LR15YC-1 or Bosch WR7DCX (8-valve) · gap 1.0–1.15 mm
items.note: Those are the plugs listed for the injected 8-valve 21214; check older carbureted engines in your manual.

items.spec: Ethylene-glycol antifreeze (Tosol or G-48 type in the factory list) · 10.7 L (≈11.3 US qt) including the heater
items.note: AvtoVAZ says not to mix different brands of antifreeze.
AvtoVAZ approves API GL-5 gear oil: 75W-90, 80W-90 or 85W-90 depending on climate. The schedule also changes all gear oils at the first 2,000 km.
Use both levers regularly so the centre-lock mechanism doesn't seize, especially in winter.

items.interval: Every 40,000 km (≈24,900 mi); check levels every 10,000 km
items.note: Look for weeping axle seals at the rear and leaks where the front differential meets the engine.
The box uses gear oil even on trucks with power steering; the power-steering reservoir (1.7 L) is separate. Check its fluid type in your manual.

items.spec: DOT 4-class fluid (factory list: Rosdot, Torsa DOT-4) · brakes 0.535 L, clutch 0.2 L
items.note: The clutch is hydraulic and shares the fluid type. Bleed both circuits.

items.spec: Adjustable taper bearings on pre-October-2016 trucks
items.interval: Check play at every service; repack and adjust at 40,000 km
items.note: Trucks built from October 2016 have bearings that don't need adjusting.

items.spec: Grease the crosses and slip splines
items.note: Not needed on CV-jointed shafts. Dry splines and joints are a common cause of the Niva shake.

items.interval: Check condition and tension at every service
items.note: BaT sellers report charging problems on imports, so test the battery and alternator output.

parts.name: Gates alternator & P/S belt kit, Niva 2121/2131

items.spec: Clear the sill, door and front-wing drain holes; wax the cavities
items.interval: Drains at every service; anti-corrosion inspection yearly
items.note: This is in AvtoVAZ's own schedule, because the body is the chassis.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: About 27–27.5 inches. Stock is 185/75R16 (175/80R16 on early trucks), roughly 26.9–27.0 in tall. NIVA-FAQ owners report that on 15-inch wheels a 205/70R15 clears on the right offset, but a 205/75R15 rubs the front of the arch at full lock and the rear arch at full droop. Size for size, a 205/70R16 (27.3 in) is about the limit. The factory Bronto runs 235/75R16s, but only with 35 mm more ground clearance. BaT's 1993 Niva on oversized 15s 'rubs on the wheel wells'.

No. It has a steel unibody with the suspension bolted to it, and Wikipedia calls it the world's first mass-produced off-roader built that way. That's why rust in the sills and floor matters so much more than on a framed truck.

faq.q: Can I leave the centre diff locked?
faq.a: Not on pavement. AvtoVAZ says to lock it before a difficult section, not while the wheels are already spinning, and to unlock it on good roads, because driving locked wears the drivetrain and tyres and can cause a skid under braking. High-to-low and the centre lock can be selected on the move with the clutch down, but low range should be selected at a standstill. If the lock won't engage, NIVA-FAQ suggests turning the wheel slightly while pulling the lever. If it won't release, weave the steering on a straight, or stop and reverse a little while pushing the lever forward.

faq.q: Can I import one into the US?
faq.a: Yes, once it's 25 years old, counted from its date of manufacture. As of October 2026 that's anything built before late 2001. Ladas were never sold new in the US, but Canada sold the Niva from the 1981 to the 1998 model year, and BaT's US Nivas came from Spain, the Netherlands, Estonia and Russia. Russian-made goods have been charged at higher 'Column 2' duty rates since 2022, so ask a customs broker before you buy.

faq.q: Does it have a timing belt?
faq.a: Not the 1.6 and 1.7 petrol engines in every US-eligible Niva: they use a timing chain. The known weak spot is the tensioner and its guide shoe, which rattle when worn (see the repair section). The rare Peugeot-diesel 21215 and the 2026 1.8 are different engines, so check before you assume.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: AvtoVAZ quotes 9.9 L/100 km (≈24 mpg US) on the EU combined cycle for both the three-door and the five-door 1.7 injection, and says it's a comparison figure, not a real-world one. Its own top speeds are 142 km/h (88 mph) for the three-door and 137 km/h (85 mph) for the five-door, and the three-door needs 17 seconds to reach 100 km/h.
Not much. The 2018 manual rates both body styles at 600 kg (≈1,320 lb) braked and 300 kg (≈660 lb) unbraked, with 25–50 kg on the ball, and limits towing to 100 km/h.
AvtoVAZ says no deeper than 0.5 m (≈20 in), entering slowly so there's no bow wave at the grille, because water drawn into the air intake will wreck the engine.

faq.q: Why does my Niva vibrate at highway speed?
faq.a: Usually it's the transfer case and propshafts working against each other. Balance the wheels, grease or replace the U-joints and splines, then have the transfer case centred dynamically: loosen its mounts, run the truck at the speed where it shakes, and retighten. On a VAZ-2121 the height has to be shimmed first. Worn rubber mounts or a damaged floor can also cause it.

The classic budget lift is longer GAZ Volga front springs cut down by two coils, 25 mm spacers between the upper arms and the upper ball joints, and spacers under the rear springs. One NIVA-FAQ owner measured about 45–60 mm more at the front that way. Off-the-shelf kits such as CreativeGarage's Newbie Hard promise 45–55 mm. Raised coils are also sold for 1983–98 trucks. The factory did its own: the 2017 Bronto sits 35 mm higher on 235/75R16s.

faq.q: Which years should I look for?
faq.a: In the US, only trucks over 25 years old can be imported, so the choice is a 1.6 VAZ-2121 (four-speed, through 1993) or an early 1.7 21213 or 21214 (five-speed, from 1993–94). The 1.7s are torquier and have the low-lip tailgate, while the pre-1985 trucks with chrome trim are the collector pieces. Wikipedia mentions a 1980 truck that sold in Russia for 3.2 million roubles in 2016. Elsewhere, the 2009–2011 21214M updates, ABS from late 2011 and the maintenance-free hubs from October 2016 make later trucks easier to live with. Whatever the year, the best Niva is the least rusty one.

By modern standards, no. Russia's ARCAP gave a 21213 zero stars in a 2002 frontal crash test, and the glovebox hit the passenger dummy hard enough to risk a brain injury. Wikipedia said in 2019 that no version had airbags; the 2026 update finally adds one for the driver. Drive it like the 1970s design it is.

mods.why: A 45–55 mm lift and fresh springs make room for 27-inch-plus tyres and recover sag. Spacer kits are the bolt-on route; raised coils replace tired springs.
